messages:
alyssa: quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak i see a small host-side perf regression on short text requests. p50 fine, p95/p99 shifted up. attaching profile snippets below

maria: thanks. is this on the grpc ingress or the http path?

alyssa: grpc only so far. looks correlated with 'select_kernel(vfast -> vfast+fuse)' path. CPU samples show extra time in parse/tokenize stage once we land the new kernel vote.

chris: can you paste the flame?

alyssa: paste: ````
CPU samples (cold):
  - host_parse_tokenize: 28%
  - proto_unmarshal: 12%
  - kernel_selection: 6%
  - kv_cache_lookup: 4%
After change:
  - host_parse_tokenize: 36%
  - proto_unmarshal: 10%
  - kernel_selection: 2%
  - kv_cache_lookup: 4%
````

devon: interesting — kernel_selection time dropped but parse jumped. maybe the new kernel increases pressure on small-frame handling and causes extra memcpy in the ingress framer.

maria: i also saw an uptick in small write syscalls in the tracer: more writev() calls per request. could be chunking logic emitting smaller frames after kernel vote changes.

alyssa: exact. grpc framing looks to split payload into more fragments when sequence length < 64 tokens -> more host-side loop iterations.

chris: do we have a reproducer? small echo request ~20 tokens?

alyssa: repro steps: curl -> grpc gateway -> model route with kernel=vfast+fuse, sample prompt ~20 tokens. p99 baseline ~48ms, with change ~65ms.

devon: i pushed a tiny instrument to count frame sizes and writev counts on the proxy side. preliminary: avg writev per request went 1.3 -> 2.1, avg bytes/frame dropped ~1.8x.

maria: ok, so two levers: 1) change chunking heuristic to prefer single-frame for short sequences, 2) amortize tokenization work across batched requests (if batching allowed).

alyssa: batching helps but these are often single-request interactive calls. prefer to optimizer host path: bump coalesce window to 2ms for grpc small writes + prefer in-place tokenization to avoid extra copies.

chris: small note — in-place tokenize touches the buffer and currently violates assumptions for zero-copy proto parsing. need to be careful with ownership.

devon: alternative: add a small fast-path in ingress: if payload_length < 512 && tokens < 40 -> single-frame and skip split. cheap check.

alyssa: good idea. also KV cache: profiler shows a bit more thrash on hits because of extra key normalization step triggered by fused kernel path. 2 extra string allocations on hit path.

maria: can we short-circuit normalization for host-side cache hits? we already compute a canonical key in the gateway earlier in flow for routing. maybe reuse that.

chris: reuseable, but need to thread the canonical_key through the request meta — small patch.

devon: i'll prototype the single-frame heuristic + canonical_key pass-through in a PR. estimate: 1 day for prototype, 1 day for perf + canary.

alyssa: thanks. i can run microbenchmarks and collect p50/p95/p99 before/after. also will capture writev counts and allocation samples.

infra-bot: perf alert acknowledged by alyssa. linked ticket: INF-2194

maria: one more thought — kernel selector change was intended to reduce decode tail; we should validate that we didn't regress tokenization cost by adding post-selection transforms. maybe we can push more work into kernel selection stage so runtime path is lighter.

chris: agree. long-term, consider moving small-frame heuristics into selector so selection emits a hint: CHUNK_POLICY=single|multi. avoids back-and-forth.

alyssa: action items:
  - devon: prototype single-frame heuristic on ingress (PR)
  - chris: add canonical_key passthrough patch
  - alyssa: run microbench and post results (p50/p95/p99, writev counts, allocs)
  - maria: validate that kernel selector changes are not introducing extra allocation/transforms

chris: will assign reviewers: @maria, @alyssa

alyssa: ping me when PRs are up. plan: canary on eng-dedicated fleet, validate 48h before rollout.

devon: starting branch now.

maria: thanks all — quick, focused fix should get p99 back in range. :thumbsup:
